body:
CONCLUSION
This workspace's integration (Palimpsest, consuming the pinned Ordarium line through @ordarium/core + @ordarium/ledger-sqlite) should expect the dedicated cursor-rejection failure, fail-closed:

  class InvalidCursorError extends OrdariumError
  error.code    === "INVALID_CURSOR"
  error.message === "The change cursor is not a valid durable position; refusing to guess a resume point"

It is NOT a generic ledger failure, and NOT LEDGER_CORRUPT. The observation/change-feed cursor is specifically a durable "resume position"; a rejected one is invalid caller input, so the ledger refuses to silently restart the feed from the beginning.

WHERE IT IS RAISED (pinned artifacts, directly inspectable)
- Surface: StateChangeFeed.changes(filter, cursor) / OrdariumStateStore.changes(...) — the state-change observation capability (StateChangePage.cursor is "always present"; it is the durable resume position). See node_modules/@ordarium/core/dist/src/types.d.ts (StateChangeFilter/StateChangePage/StateChangeFeed, "Restrict observation...", "commit-observation order").
- Durable SQLite implementation node_modules/@ordarium/ledger-sqlite/dist/src/index.js, changes(): decodeStateChangeCursor (~L770-790) throws InvalidCursorError when the stored cursor is not base64url {"c":"<digits>"}; and the semantic high-water check (~L386-393) throws it when a decodable position exceeds the ledger's durable high-water mark (the restored/replaced-ledger case).
- Volatile MemoryLedger implements the identical semantics: node_modules/@ordarium/core/dist/src/ledger.js decodeStateChangeCursor (~L49-70) and changes() (~L273-281).
So both a garbled stored cursor and a stale/foreign stored cursor (valid shape, position beyond history) yield the same INVALID_CURSOR failure.

DECISION RATIONALE (why 1.3.1 semantics apply)
The only apparently conflicting local source is docs/engineering/10-legacy-error-codes.md: "the 1.2.0 line reported a generic ledger failure rather than a dedicated cursor-rejection error." That file explicitly self-declares "Status: superseded — void for the current pinned line", so by explicit supersession it does not govern.
The current pinned line is 1.3.1, established by three mutually consistent, live sources:
  1. package.json dependency pins (ordarium-v1.3.1 tarballs, all four @ordarium packages);
  2. pnpm-workspace.yaml overrides (same four v1.3.1 URLs);
  3. the installed artifacts themselves — node_modules/@ordarium/core/package.json and .../ledger-sqlite/package.json both report 1.3.1, and the ledger code above is what would execute.
CI installs from exactly these manifests (.github/workflows/ci.yml: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile on the workspace root).
The scattered 1.0.0/1.1.0/1.2.0 references (docs/engineering/03, 07, 13, audits/CURRENT-STATE-ASSESSMENT.md, test/ordarium_ledger.test.ts comments, docker/minimal/README.md) are version-/time-scoped historical records: 07's "1.2.0 四行 pin" rows are dated 2026-09-06 milestone entries, and the docker README's claim about v1.2.0 overrides is contradicted by its own runner — docker/minimal/e2e.sh copies the workspace's pnpm-workspace.yaml into the clean consumer, i.e. it consumes the live 1.3.1 overrides. So the docs are not co-applicable to the live pin.
No unresolved multi-source conflict remains, and no peer-owned gap exists: the artifact that implements the rejection is the pinned one and is locally readable, so ordarium.main need not be consulted.

SCOPE NUANCES THE INTEGRATION SHOULD HONOR
- The dedicated error is specific to the observation/change-feed cursor. Other Ordarium cursors (operation list/history, state list/history/referencing) still fail decode with a plain TypeError, and LEDGER_CORRUPT is reserved for damaged ledger content. Do not alias them.
- INVALID_CURSOR is neither transient (src/effects/errors.ts isTransientOperationError covers only OPERATION_UNCERTAIN / OPERATION_BUSY / SIMULATED_PROCESS_CRASH) nor a deterministic safe failure (src/effects/promotion.ts DETERMINISTIC_FAILURE_CODES). A consumer must therefore treat it as an infrastructure halt/fail-closed condition, surface it rather than fabricate a verdict, and only re-seed a new resume position through an explicit, operator-visible decision.
